headline: Pidilite Industries hikes Fevicol prices; Bombay HC sets aside ICICI Bank board's sanction order.

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Pidilite Industries announced a price hike of up to 7% for Fevicol starting December 1.
The Bombay High Court set aside a sanction order by the ICICI Bank board against Chanda Kochhar.
India imposed a 162.5% duty on bulk Scotch imports due to trade pact disputes with the UK.
CEA Nageswaran warned that Rupee strength could pose economic challenges for India by FY28.
whatHappening: Pidilite is increasing prices on its flagship adhesive brand to manage rising costs.
Legal developments regarding ICICI Bank's former leadership are being monitored by investors.
Tata Sons board members are scheduled to review Air India's performance on November 19.
IndoSpace has expanded its industrial and logistics footprint with a new park in Karnataka.
summary: Pidilite Industries is raising Fevicol prices by 7%, while ICICI Bank faces a court ruling regarding its former CEO. Trade tensions with the UK have led to high duties on Scotch imports, impacting trade dynamics. Tata Sons is set to review Air India's performance as industrial expansion continues in Karnataka.
